title: Session 10 – Marketing Planning and Resource Allocation: Applications of Regression Analysis

blocks.text: Recap: regression answers questions about relationships and predictions (y = b0 + b1x + ε). The intercept is the estimated y at x = 0; a significant b-coefficient is the change in y for a one-unit change in x; R² is the share of explained variance.
A causal effect requires that x precedes y, that x is reliably correlated with y, and that the relation is not explained by other causes.
A coefficient must be read as an association if x is (potentially) endogenous:
A coefficient can be interpreted causally if x is exogenous (manipulated by an external force). Only causal effects justify policy recommendations; beware spurious correlations.

children: Marketing mix decision: which factors are associated with Airbnb prices in New York?
Spending pattern optimisation: grocery spending – descriptives, dummies, scatter plot, hypotheses, multiple regression, refined model, prediction
Sales forecast: movie box office with budget, runtime and rating ("1917")

blocks.text: In the exam, regression tables are interpreted step by step: significance → strongest effects → recommendations (advertising, product) → limitations and improvements.
An independent variable that may be correlated with the error term (e.g. due to reverse causality or omitted variables) – its coefficient is only an association.
An independent variable determined outside the model, e.g. manipulated by an external force – its coefficient can be interpreted causally.
A statistical association between two variables without a causal link.
